transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess it’s little mistakes that keep happening. I’ll write the wrong time on a senior-center class sheet, or measure a board and still cut it a bit short because I missed the small print. Things like that.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I have quiet days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in things.
Do you ever feel like you can't enjoy things, even the things you used to like?
No… I don’t think so. I still enjoy the things I usually like. Maybe I’m not always very energetic about them, but I wouldn’t say I can’t enjoy them.
Have you ever experienced things that others don’t seem to experience, like hearing voices when no one is around or seeing things that others don’t see?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t had anything like that, not that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down or having trouble feeling motivated, even if you still enjoy things?
I haven’t really noticed much change, no. Motivation comes and goes a bit, I guess, but nothing that feels like a big mood change.
Have you noticed any difficulties with your memory or thinking clearly lately?

A little, I guess. Mostly I misplace things—keys, my reading glasses, little things like that. I’ll have just had them in my hand and then spend too long looking for them. It’s annoying, but… I don’t know if that counts as memory exactly.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to plan, organize, or follow through with tasks that used to feel straightforward?

A little, yeah. If I’ve got a few things on the same day—errands, getting the workshop ready, an appointment—I don’t always put them in the right order. I’ll start one thing, stop halfway, then end up rushing around at the end.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to remember recent events or conversations more than usual?

Not recent events so much, I don’t think. More like… my wife will tell me something, like that she moved the cards to the hall closet, and then a minute later I realize I heard her talking but I didn’t really take in where she said they were.
Do you find it hard to remember things you just learned, like someone telling you a new phone number or giving you directions to a place?

Yeah… sometimes. Like my wife will look right at me and say, “Dave, the cards are in the hall closet now,” and then a minute later I know she said something, but I can’t remember where she said they were.
Do you find it harder than before to focus on tasks, like reading a book or following a conversation, especially when there’s some background noise or distractions?

Yeah, I guess so. At the senior center, if folks are talking at the next table, or my phone lights up, I kind of… my mind goes over there. Then I’ve lost my place in whatever I was filling out or putting together.
Do you ever feel confused about where you are, what day it is, or have trouble recognizing familiar people?
No… I don’t think so. I know where I am and what day it is, and I recognize people I know. That hasn’t really been an issue.
Have you had any trouble judging distances or figuring out which direction to go, like misjudging how far away something is or getting confused with directions?
No… not really. I mean, I don’t think I’m misjudging things like that. Directions can be a little annoying sometimes, but I haven’t noticed getting confused about where to go.
Have you noticed any trouble figuring out how things fit together visually, like misplacing items in odd locations or having difficulty assembling something that used to be easy for you?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed putting things in strange places or not being able to fit things together. Nothing like that stands out.
Have you found it harder lately to manage tasks that require a few steps, like planning a meal, balancing the checkbook, or organizing a project at work?

Yeah… a bit. If I’ve got a few errands, and maybe something to get ready for at my workshop, plus an appointment, I don’t always put it in the right order. I’ll start one thing, stop, move to another… then I’m rushing at the end.
Have these difficulties been causing you any noticeable distress or making it harder for you to do things you need to do at work, at home, or with friends?

Yeah… a little. I’ve had to back off from helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops, because I don’t want to mess up the plan. And my wife’s been checking things over more, like family visits or things at the center, so I don’t throw the timing off.
Do you feel like these difficulties with memory and focus have been getting worse over time, or do they come and go depending on the situation?
I’d say it’s been more noticeable since we moved into the condo… about a year or so ago. Maybe a year and a month. Before that, I don’t think it was getting in the way as much.
Would you say these difficulties with memory and focus have affected your life in ways that feel beyond normal aging, like struggling with things you used to handle without thinking?

Yeah… I guess so. I mean, I used to handle those workshop plans without thinking much, and now I’ve had to step back from leading a couple. My wife also checks our plans more, for family visits or things at the center, so I don’t throw the timing off.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to make decisions, solve problems, or stay focused on a task for more than a few minutes?

Yeah… mostly staying focused, I guess. Like at the senior center, if people are talking at the next table, or my phone lights up, my mind kind of goes over there. Then I lose my place in whatever I was filling out or working on.
